title: 2022 AMC 12B Problem 9
statement: The sequence \(a_0,\) \(a_1,\) \(a_2,\) \(\cdots\) is a strictly increasing arithmetic sequence of positive integers such that \[2^{a_7} = 2^{27} \cdot a_7.\] What is the minimum possible value of \(a_2?\)

solutions.text:
Dividing by \(2^{27},\) we need \(2^{a_7 - 27} = a_7.\) Thus \(a_7=2^j\) and \(2^j-j=27,\) where \(j=a_7-27\ge0.\) The left side is strictly increasing for \(j\ge1,\) and \(j=5\) works, so uniquely \(a_7=32.\)

With common difference \(d \ge 1,\) we have \(a_7 = a_0 + 7d = 32\) and \(a_2 = a_0 + 2d = 32 - 5d.\) To minimize \(a_2\) we maximize \(d;\) since \(a_0 = 32 - 7d \ge 1,\) the largest choice is \(d = 4\) (giving \(a_0 = 4\)).

Then \(a_2 = 32 - 20 = 12.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Divide both sides by \(2^{27}\) to get \(2^{a_7 - 27} = a_7\)
After finding \(a_7,\) write \(a_2 = a_7 - 5d\) and make the common difference \(d\) as large as possible
